title: Fur Elise (opening motif, arranged for absolute beginners)
subtitle: 16-bar beginner arrangement: melody with a single bass note per bar
trains: The famous opening motif read at a gentle tempo with eighth notes at most, over a single left-hand bass note per bar - the hands barely need to coordinate.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Beethoven, Fur Elise, WoO 59 (public domain, composed c. 1810), opening only. The quoted bars were checked against the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond engraving (piece-info id 931, fur_Elise_WoO59.ly, typeset by Stelios Samelis from the Breitkopf & Härtel edition of 1888); the audit record content/library/audit/repertoire/beginner/fur-elise-theme-16-bar.json re-runs that check.
provenance.note: A different, much simpler arrangement from the intermediate Fur Elise item. The pickup and bars 1-8 follow Beethoven's melody with every value doubled (3/8 written as 3/4), with the changes listed in departures; bars 9-16 repeat bars 5-8. The left hand is a single sustained bass note per bar and rests under the opening figure, as in Beethoven's own texture there. 17 written measures (a one-beat pickup plus 16 bars) at quarter = 60.

departures: Metre and values: Beethoven's 3/8 is written as 3/4 with every note value doubled (sixteenths become eighths).
Bar 1: E, D-sharp (eighths), E (quarter), B, D (eighths); Beethoven has six even notes E-D#-E-B-D-C, so the C before bar 2's A is left out and no more than four equal notes follow each other.
Bars 3-4: no accidentals after bar 1 - G instead of G-sharp in bar 3, D instead of D-sharp at the end of bar 4.
Bars 5-8 are our own shortened version of Beethoven's bars 5-8: bar 5 is E, D, C, B (Beethoven: E, D-sharp, E, B, D, C), bar 7 repeats bar 3 (Beethoven: B, E, C, B), and bar 8 ends on A.
Left hand: our own single bass note per bar (A or E) instead of Beethoven's broken chords.
